# Edge-band resize: boot-pinned caps and a dead floor

## Context

Operator report on `apps/workstation` (2026-08-29): the left edge splitter can be dragged left, but **on drop the side pane snaps back to its initial width**; dragging **right does not move at all**. Both symptoms reproduced first-hand with a real pointer against the dev server, and both trace to the workstation theme's edge-band bounds — with one engine-tier parity hole underneath that turns a mis-themed floor into a silent restore instead of a clamped commit.

Live latest-open sweep: checked latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-29T18:10Z; no equivalent found. A2A claim sweep over the herd window: no competing claim on this scope.

## The Problem

Two defects, one theme block, and they contradict each other:

**1. The right-drag freeze (dead ceiling).** `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` sets `--dock-edge-band-left-max-inline-size: 16.25rem` (260px). The committed document boots the left edge at `extent: 0.20`, which the projection paints as inline `width: 20%` — 315px in a 1576px row. CSS clamps the render to 260px, so **the band boots already pinned at its own max**. `Neo.main.draggable.Resize#createState` folds computed CSS min/max into the clamp window, giving `maxSize === startSize` → every rightward frame clamps to the start value → zero movement. Measured: a +228px rightward drag stops at exactly 260px.

The constants are 1280px-era: `20.3125cqi × 1280 = 260px = 16.25rem` exactly — the trio was authored as a *preferred-width* `clamp(11.25rem, 20.3125cqi, 16.25rem)` for static chrome, and PR #17845 unfolded it into real `min`/`max` custom properties so the new resize contract could read them. Numerically faithful, semantically different: the clamp's upper arm meant "preferred width tops out here"; a `max-inline-size` means "the user may never go past here". At any dock host wider than 1300px the left band boots with zero rightward headroom. Same for the other edges: right band boots pinned at its 320px max (`25% > 20rem`), bottom at its 200px max (`25% > 12.5rem`).

**2. The drop-restore (dead floor).** The same theme file also carries `.workstation-workspace .neo-dashboard-dock-edge-band { min-height: 0; min-width: 0 }` — the classic flex min-content fix. Its physical properties out-cascade the engine's logical `min-inline-size: var(..., 11.25rem)` band rule (specificity 0,2,0 vs 0,1,0), so the intended 180px floor **computes to 0**. A decisive leftward drag previews the band down to `0px` (it visually vanishes mid-gesture), the terminal reports `resizeSize: 0`, `DockSplitter#resolveEdgeExtent` yields extent `0`, and `Operations.resizeEdgeZone` refuses it — the validation domain is the **open** interval `(0,1)`. The refusal settles the main thread with `restore: true`, which writes back the pre-gesture inline style: the operator's "restores the initial width". Measured: far-left drag → immediate `width: 0px` → settled back to the pre-gesture percentage.

Moderate drags inside the live corridor commit exactly (190px → `12.0558%`; 260px → `16.4975%`) — the resize machinery itself (#17845 settlement + #17849 terminal parity) is healthy. The corridor is just wrong on both ends.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` — `.neo-dashboard-dock-edge-band {min-height: 0; min-width: 0}` (the floor-killer) and the `--dock-edge-band-*-{max,min}-*` var trio on `.workstation-dock-host`.
- `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:422-448` — the engine band rules: `min/max-inline-size` (left/right) and `min/max-block-size` (top/bottom) read the per-edge vars with engine defaults `min 8rem/6rem`, **`max 50%`**. The dock host is a `container-type: size` container, so `cqi`/`cqb` terms resolve against it.
- `src/main/draggable/Resize.mjs#createState` — the clamp window comes exclusively from the target's computed CSS bounds; a consumer that zeroes the floor lets the preview paint a state the model categorically refuses.
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/DockSplitter.mjs#getResizeConfig` (edge branch) + `#resolveEdgeExtent` + `Operations.resizeEdgeZone` (open-interval validation) — the refusal → `settleMainThreadResize(restore: true)` → exact snapshot restore.

## The Fix

**App tier (the defect):** in `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss`
1. Replace the blanket `min-height: 0; min-width: 0` on `.neo-dashboard-dock-edge-band` with **cross-axis-only** zeroing (`min-height: 0` for left/right bands, `min-width: 0` for top/bottom). The drag axis then carries the engine floor vars again — a full-left drag clamps at 11.25rem and commits, instead of collapsing to 0 and being refused.
2. Drop the three `--dock-edge-band-*-max-*` overrides. The caps no longer serve their original purpose (boot width is governed by the document extent's inline style, not the preferred-width var); today they only limit user drags. Removing them lands on the engine default `50%` cap — a container-relative bound on **each individual edge**, not an aggregate center reservation (opposing edges dragged to their caps can meet in the middle; the reviewer's control measures `{left: 500, center: 0, right: 500}` for a 1000px row with two 50% bands), unpinned at every size. *(Wording corrected per PR #17858 review RA-2, 2026-08-29.)*

**Engine tier (the parity hole):** the preview must never paint a state the semantic commit categorically refuses. The edge branch of `DockSplitter#getResizeConfig` gains a commit-domain floor (`minSize: 1`), and `Resize#createState` folds `config.minSize` into the clamp window. With this, even a consumer whose CSS zeroes the floor gets a 1px-clamped preview whose terminal commits (`extent > 0`), never a silent restore. `layoutMax` already keeps `extent < 1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Workstation left/right/bottom edge splitters drag in **both** directions from boot at desktop widths; outward drags are capped by the engine's 50% default, inward drags clamp at the theme floors and **commit** there.
- [ ] The full-collapse restore is gone: no reachable pointer position on an edge splitter produces a refused `resizeEdgeZone` commit in workstation.
- [ ] Edge descriptor carries the commit-domain floor: unit-tier witness that the edge branch emits `minSize: 1` alongside `awaitWorkerSettlement: true`.
- [ ] Component-tier (real main thread) witness: with a target whose CSS min is 0, a far-inward drag clamps at the descriptor floor and the terminal **commits** (no `restore: true` settle).
- [ ] Cross-axis flex fix retained: bands still shrink on their cross axis (no min-content overflow regression in the stacked rows).

## Out of Scope

- Re-deriving workstation's *preferred* band sizes (`20.3125cqi` etc.) — they are shadowed by document extents at runtime; harmless.
- Whitebox NL journey extension for edge drags (`WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL` both-direction tour) — rides the #17844 journey lane; e2e runs in no CI (per the #17853 resolution), so this ticket's teeth are unit/component tier.
- Boot divergence normalization (document `extent: 0.20` vs CSS-clamped paint): removing the caps dissolves the common case; floor-pinned boot at very narrow windows commits truthfully on first drag.

## Decision Record impact

aligned-with ADR 0029 (docking design): preview-commit parity — the committed vector equals the final preview by construction — is the design value the engine-tier floor completes for the refusal domain.
